requests.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: Victoria 3 painted technology icon. Image 1 is the existing EDIT TARGET. Change only the correspondence papers as requested: the top sealed envelope must be clean white paper with NO writing anywhere on its exterior, including its triangular folded flap. Keep the burgundy wax seal visibly closing this blank envelope. Put one or two loose white sheets UNDER the envelope, with exposed portions bearing subtle dark handwritten lines: the writing belongs only to these unsealed underlying sheets, never to the closed envelope. No need for an address; leave the envelope entirely blank. Preserve the existing diagonal dark feather quill, red wax seal motif, natural white-paper material, brushwork, restrained highlights, elevated three-quarter viewpoint and compact readable technology-icon silhouette. Minor paper overlap adjustment is allowed to expose the written sheets clearly. No invented extra props. Entire feather, nib and paper corners must fit inside a square canvas at least 1024 pixels with small transparent margins; nothing cropped. Genuine transparent alpha background, including gaps between objects and all four canvas corners with alpha zero. No floor, tabletop, opaque backdrop, frame, medallion, halo, watermark, logo, decorative text or numbers. Handwriting on loose sheets should suggest correspondence without readable words. Do not apply sepia tint or blue color cast.

Use case: compositing. Asset type: Victoria 3 painted experimental-research technology icon. Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and establishes the painted style, glassware, palette and light. Image 2 is ONLY a form reference for the additional antique brass microscope; it is not a style or background reference. Add a painted version of this microscope NEXT TO the existing alembic/retort glassware, as an additional clearly identifiable instrument. Follow the photographed microscope's tall brass tube, focus knobs, small sample stage, circular angled mirror under the stage and dark metal foot. Omit the photograph's large wooden storage boxes, spare parts and studio background. Preserve both glassware subjects from Image 1: the squat three-neck blue-green Woulfe bottle with corks and curved tubes, and the smaller spherical swan-neck retort with a little amber liquid. Their assembly is an illustrative convention, not a certified exact reconstruction. Reposition and reduce the two glass objects slightly if necessary to make room for the microscope within one compact balanced group; do not cover the microscope's stage or mirror, or hide the three bottle necks. The microscope should be large enough to read at 48/64 pixels, beside rather than inside a glass vessel. Match all three objects with the same hand-painted volumetric brushwork, matte material highlights, restrained natural brass, gray-black foot, teal-gray glass and warm cork. Preserve the existing visual family, not a photographic collage and not a gold monochrome PM glyph. Center the complete group on a square canvas at least 1024 pixels with transparent margins; all tube ends, eyepiece, feet and flask bottoms fully visible, not clipped. Genuine transparent alpha background, transparent open gaps between microscope parts and glass tubes, and all four canvas corners with alpha zero. No room, tabletop, floor, solid black/gray background, backing disc, frame, medallion, glow, text, labels, numbers, watermark or logo. No modern binocular microscope, electricity, rubber hoses, Bunsen burner or Erlenmeyer flask. No blue color cast or uniform sepia filter. Only the requested microscope may be added.
